In a series of running gags, Robert Stack's character Captain Rex Kramer strides through the airport terminal repeatedly punching, shoving, and otherwise brutalizing a parade of solicitors trying to hand him pamphlets and flowers. The joke landed for 1980 American audiences with a force it does not have for younger viewers today, because of a then-ubiquitous fixture of US airport terminals: members of X, a particular spiritual movement, founded in New York in 1966 by Y, who would station themselves at airports to chant, distribute literature, and solicit donations. ID X (10 points) and Y (10 points).
Answers: X=Hare Krishna/ISKCON, Y= A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada

9.	X was the first lady of the American musical theater. Across a career spanning almost five decades on Broadway, she introduced more enduring standards from the Great American Songbook than perhaps any other performer — songs by Cole Porter, Irving Berlin, the Gershwins, and Jule Styne. Her voice was so famously powerful she rarely needed amplification on stage. In a brief, surreal cameo in _Airplane!_, she plays a male WWII war veteran in a hospital bed who believes he is, in fact, X — sitting up in full wig and makeup to belt out “Everything's Coming Up Roses” from her 1959 Broadway smash _Gypsy_. _ Airplane!_ was X's final on-screen appearance before her death in 1984. ID X (10 points).
